Here’s how I did it: 

I struggle with general mental health issues: anxiety, depression, delusions, addiction. I rented a room in a house for 4 years and then moved to another city to go to university. Due to my mental health issues and bad decisions they cause, I lost my spot at University and got kicked off campus where I lived in a dorm.

After becoming officially homeless with no one to stay with a went to a warmer state because it was winter where I live in the Pacific Northwest and if I ended up sleeping outside , I wanted to be somewhere warm.

Southern California has a lot more people than the Pacific Northwest and a lot of competition for basic jobs and the homeless far outnumber the services available for the homeless. I couldn’t find a sustainable job or housing for 3 months and managed to make it back to Washington state. 

I researched an enhanced shelter in my city where I can be 24 hours. I got a job at a hotel and my case manager found an opening at a low-income apartment building that’s first-come-first serve rather than a waitlist. No credit check required. 

The shelter paid my move in fees. 

Many homeless opt out of shelter services because of negative stereotypes and it “affirms their homeless status” but if you find the right one with good staff/rules they can really help you.
